source.title: The Universal Normal Embedding
source.authors: Chen Tasker; Roy Betser; Eyal Gofer; M. Levi; Guy Gilboa

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. No apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether generative-model latents and vision-encoder embeddings can be aligned and retain shared structure using ridge-regularized linear maps and a multiview shared-space analysis. These are different measurements from the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
record.gate_note: The study directly tests linear cross-family mapping and shared latent structure. Prior-work alignment results cited in the paper were not extracted. Gaussianity tests, attribute probes, and editing results do not measure convergence or interchangeability and are not included as rows. Supplementary scale results concern attribute classification, not representational alignment.
record.test_reason: The study fits ridge-regularized linear maps from DDIM-inverted latents of three diffusion models (SD 1.5, SD 2.1, LCM) into three encoder spaces (CLIP B16, OpenCLIP L14, DINOv3), using paired CelebA images. It reports MSE, cosine similarity and the accuracy drop of fixed encoder classifiers (Table 2). This tests V4, cross-family linear interchangeability, with a different method from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that DDIM-inverted noise and encoder embeddings carry comparable, linearly decodable semantics, can be linearly aligned with negligible accuracy loss, and support linear edits. They offer this as preliminary evidence that both are noisy linear projections of a shared approximately Gaussian latent space (UNE).
record.recipe_differences: The study tests a related shared-geometry claim using paired-data ridge mappings, attribute-transfer evaluations, and a multiview shared-space estimator; it does not reproduce the original measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment is evaluated for three target encoders (CLIP B16, OpenCLIP L14, DINOv3) and three diffusion models (SD 1.5, SD 2.1, LCM), with distinct MSE, cosine-similarity, and accuracy-drop results. Transfer mappings are learned on paired samples.

fits_no_version.finding: GCCA shared spaces built from different mixes of encoder and diffusion latents produce highly correlated neighborhood similarity vectors (Spearman, figure only). At 16 dimensions they classify attributes as well as single-model PCA spaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A low-dimensional shared subspace recovered jointly from encoders and generators preserves common neighborhood and attribute structure.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear-probe attribute accuracies on DDIM-inverted noise correlate highly per attribute with CLIP-B/16 probe accuracies (Fig. 3b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different model families make the same semantic attributes linearly decodable, with matching per-attribute difficulty.

record.problems: The transfer evaluation uses paired CelebA samples and does not test unpaired mapping or generalization of alignment to other datasets. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the Table 2 results. The shared-space neighborhood correlations are only available as a figure, with no values stated in the text. The scale comparison concerns attribute separability rather than alignment.
record.rows_left_out: Supplementary Figure 9 compares attribute-classification AUC across pixel space, SD 1.5, SD 1.5 fine-tuned on CelebA, CelebA Diff, and SDXL. The text reports that the smaller model degrades, scale gives only marginal improvement, and CelebA fine-tuning reduces separability. These results do not measure cross-model alignment, so they were not extracted as claim-version rows.

untested.parts: Stitching layers, relative representations, and mapping without paired data. Mapping between encoders, or the reverse direction (encoder to generator). Datasets other than CelebA (the AFHQ supplement tests classification only, not transfer).
Alignment versus model scale or capability is not measured. The SDXL comparison in Supp. Fig. 9 concerns attribute AUC, not alignment.
No comparison of recurring features or circuits.
No variation of metric, settings or input distribution for alignment.
No test of plateau or cause. All diffusion models are from the SD family, which shares training data, but this is not examined.

missing.what: Per-attribute probe accuracy agreement between diffusion noise latents and encoders. It is related to shared structure, though not a mapping result.
Numeric Spearman correlations between shared spaces X1–X5.

record.verdict_notes: The study uses only CelebA, paired data, a single ridge alpha, no uncertainty estimates, and no unmapped or random-map baseline for MSE or cosine. So 'low' and 'high' are the authors' judgments, not comparisons to a control. Diffusion latents are about 16k dimensions, mapped to 512–768 dimensions. The accuracy-drop baseline (native encoder accuracy) is not given numerically. The study is not an original source, so verdicts are allowed.

versions.untested_parts: No measurement of whether independently trained models become more aligned as scale or capability increases. The supplementary scale comparison concerns attribute-classification performance, not alignment.
No comparison of image representations with paired caption or language-model representations, or of alignment as both modalities improve.

Linear transfer is tested between DDIM-inverted diffusion latents and encoder embeddings using paired images. The study does not test stitching layers, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
The study reports multiple alignment metrics but does not test whether convergence changes with metric settings, input choice, or out-of-distribution data.
The study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives cause it. The tested alignment uses paired samples from CelebA.

rows.subject: Shared latent spaces X1–X5 (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: X1–X4 combine four latent sources each; X5 combines six
rows.operation_detail: Compare cosine-similarity neighborhood vectors across shared spaces using Spearman rank correlation
rows.measure: Spearman rank correlation between similarity vectors
rows.note: The text says correlations are consistently high and indicate similar neighborhood structure; numerical correlations are only shown in the figure.
rows.check: This row correlates neighborhoods across GCCA shared spaces X1–X5, which share source models (e.g. X5 contains most of X3's sources). It does not measure mapping one model onto another, and the overlap partly forces agreement by construction. Values are figure-only.

relationships.condition: Diffusion latents linearly mapped to CLIP B16 and OpenCLIP L14 (paired CelebA, ridge)
relationships.reason: Cosine is 0.72–0.81 and accuracy drop at most 0.23 pp with fixed target classifiers (T2-01–T2-06, T2-10–T2-15, T2-19–T2-24).
relationships.display_finding: Mapped representations achieved cosine 0.72–0.81 while fixed target classifiers lost at most 0.23 percentage points of accuracy.

relationships.condition: Geometric fidelity of mapping into DINOv3 (image-only self-supervised encoder)
relationships.reason: Mapped-latent cosine is only 0.54–0.57 versus 0.72–0.81 for the CLIP targets (T2-07, T2-08, T2-16, T2-17, T2-25, T2-26). Attribute information transfers, but the embedding itself is reconstructed only partially.
relationships.display_finding: Mapped-latent cosine was 0.54–0.57 for DINOv3 versus 0.72–0.81 for CLIP targets, indicating partial embedding reconstruction despite attribute transfer.

relation.reason: The study reports its own cross-model mapping fidelity and downstream preservation results.

tranche.reason: Paired-data ridge mappings and fixed-classifier transfer directly test V4 using a different method for the shared-representation question.

source_check.notes: Results concern paired CelebA mappings and 40 attribute classifiers; preserved readout accuracy does not establish complete embedding reconstruction. The authors present UNE as a hypothesis with preliminary empirical support.

statements.correction: Table 2: DINOv3 mapped cosine = 0.55 (SD 1.5), 0.54 (SD 2.1), 0.57 (LCM); fixed-classifier accuracy drops = 0.23, 0.20, 0.00 pp, respectively. Geometric-fidelity verdict = limits_scope.
statements.problem: The numbers and partial-reconstruction interpretation are supported, but the challenges label overstates this study: transfer is incomplete geometrically, not absent or reversed.
